interaction.content: Hi
Hi, how have you been lately? Is there anything you’d like help with?

Honestly, my feelings have been pretty mixed lately. I’ve been with my boyfriend for over a year now, and we were really happy, but his mom was recently diagnosed with late-stage lung cancer, and things have gotten kind of tricky.
It sounds like both of you are under a lot of pressure right now. Could you share with me some of the specific ways these things have been affecting your life and your relationship?

Ever since his mom got sick, we’ve hardly gone out at all. Every day we just head straight home at a certain time to help out. I’ve also been trying to do whatever I can at their place. Originally his mom suggested we get married earlier, but now there are some issues.
It really has gotten more complicated. You mentioned there are some issues now—what kind of problems are bothering you?

His parents said they’re willing to give us 150,000 as the betrothal gift, but we’d be responsible for renovating the house. I talked it over with my parents, but they feel 150,000 isn’t enough to cover the renovation costs, and that’s put me in a really tough spot.
I can understand why you’re feeling so troubled right now; it really does put you in a tough spot. Have you talked this over with your boyfriend in detail? What are his thoughts about it?

We’ve talked about it, and he also hopes we can get married sooner, but right now his mom’s illness is really serious and a lot of things are uncertain. He also feels that 150,000 isn’t enough to renovate, but he wants me to persuade my parents.

It sounds like the pressure you’re all under right now is really intense. If you were to talk with your parents about this again, what do you think might help you express your feelings and what you need from them?

I’m thinking I could first explain to them that the foundation of our relationship is really solid, and also tell them that because of his mom’s illness we’re hoping to get married a bit earlier, and that we really hope they can understand and support that. And of course, we can also talk about whether there’s some kind of compromise we could find.

That’s a really good idea. Being able to honestly share your feelings and the difficulties you’re facing is very important. Have you thought any further about what kinds of compromise or middle-ground solutions you might be able to discuss with your parents?

I’ve actually been thinking too, maybe we could first raise some money, or we ourselves could try to save for a while and put some of that aside for the renovation costs. Another idea is, maybe we could just do a simple renovation first and then gradually improve things later. That way the pressure would be a bit lighter for everyone.

These sound like some workable solutions that could help both sides feel understood and respected. Finding ways to raise money and save could give you two more independence, and you could also think about a simpler renovation, so you can get married earlier without such heavy financial pressure. How would you feel about talking these options over with your parents and your boyfriend?

I think I can try talking with them about these options. I am a bit worried about how they’ll react, but I still want to express what I think, and I also hope we can find a solution that everyone can accept.

That’s a really positive attitude. Being able to talk openly can help you find a solution that everyone can accept. You might choose a time when everyone is relatively relaxed to have the conversation, so it can go more smoothly. I hope you’re able to work through these issues, and if anything comes up, you can always come back and talk with me.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll look for a good time to talk with them. If there’s any new progress or if I run into any problems, I’ll come back and talk with you.
I’m glad I could be of help. I wish you all the best with your conversation, and if you need anything, feel free to come back and talk with me anytime.
Thank you for your support. I’ll do my best. If I need to, I’ll definitely come back.
You’re very welcome. You’re always welcome to come back. I’m rooting for you.

interaction.content: Hi
Hi, I’m Xiaotian. How’s your day going today?
It’s okay, I guess. I’m actually feeling a bit low today. I don’t even know why, I just feel this heaviness in my chest, like something is about to burst out.
It sounds like your emotions are a bit unsettled right now. Has anything happened recently that you’ve been especially concerned about?

It’s not like there’s some huge major event or anything, it’s just that ever since 6th grade I’ve always had this feeling. Recently, since starting 8th grade, I went online to look into what might be going on with me, and I ended up doing a test. My total score was 263, the standard score was 329, and it said my somatization is pretty serious.
I see. How do you feel about these test results?

I’d say it feels pretty accurate. I’ve always felt like I can’t catch my breath, and sometimes my whole body just feels exhausted, with back pain and headaches. I also can’t really get interested in a lot of things. So the test results seem to match my situation quite well.
These physical and emotional symptoms really could be related to your psychological state. Do you remember when this feeling first started, and what was going on around that time?
I think it first started around sixth grade. I can’t really say what exactly triggered it, it just suddenly felt that way.

I hear you. It sounds like these feelings have been affecting you for a long time. How have you been coping with this discomfort? Is there anything you do, or any activities, that help you feel a bit better, even just for a while?
I’ve tried a lot of things, like screaming, hiking, going out to have fun, but none of them really worked. Every time I’m by myself, I still feel really weighed down.
That feeling of being so bottled up really is hard to shake, and it’s tough to handle all on your own. Have you talked with any friends or family about this? How did they respond?
No. Even when I’m in a bad mood I don’t show it. I always pretend to be really happy. So they don’t know I have these problems.

It really is exhausting to keep all these feelings bottled up inside. Have you ever tried writing down how you feel, or expressing it through drawing? Sometimes those kinds of ways can also help us release some of the emotions we’ve been holding in.
I didn’t really keep track in any special way, and I don’t remember many of the feelings. I sometimes draw, but it still feels like I can’t fully let out all those pent-up emotions.

Drawing really is a great way to express yourself, but it sounds like your feelings of being held back or suppressed run pretty deep. Would you be interested in trying to make those feelings more concrete—like giving them names, or describing them in a more vivid, image-like way—to see if that brings up any new insights?

I haven’t really tried to make these feelings more concrete. I just feel like there’s something in my chest that wants to come out, but it doesn’t have a shape. If I have to describe it, maybe it’s all those pent‑up emotions.
Would you be interested in trying to give this “thing” a name or an image? That might help you understand and work with these feelings more clearly.
I can give it a try. I feel like it’s this “dark shadow” trapped in my chest, so let’s just call it the “dark shadow” for now.
Let’s call it a “dark shadow” for now. When this “dark shadow” shows up, what do you feel specifically? For example, what happens in your body, or emotionally?

When the “dark shadow” shows up, I feel this heavy pressure in my chest, like I can’t breathe. Sometimes I also feel totally drained, with headaches and back pain, and my mood sinks really low. I just lose interest in everything.

These symptoms do sound really uncomfortable for you. Have you noticed in what kinds of situations the “dark shadow” tends to show up more easily? For example, what kind of context are you usually in, or what tends to happen right before it appears?

It feels like the “shadow” shows up more easily when I’m in a bad mood. Sometimes there isn’t even any particular reason, I just suddenly feel really weighed down for no reason, and then the “shadow” comes.

It sounds like this “shadow” is connected to your mood swings. When do you tend to feel a bit better, or what kinds of things help lift your mood? Is there anything in particular that seems to ease these symptoms for you?

Sometimes hanging out with friends or doing things I enjoy, like drawing or watching anime, makes me feel a bit better, but it only seems to ease things for a while. Before long, the “dark shadow” comes back again.

Those activities can definitely help you feel relaxed for a while, but it may take a more systematic approach to really work through this. What would you like to get out of counseling, or what are you hoping for?

I hope I can find a way to completely get rid of this suffocating feeling, to stop always feeling like there’s a “dark shadow” on my chest, and to stop using self-harm to feel pleasure and a sense of being real. I want to be able to feel happy, and not be so full of self-doubt and inferiority anymore.

I hear you—you’re hoping that through counseling you can find more effective ways to deal with this sense of being weighed down and also feel better about yourself. Next, we can explore some concrete steps and strategies together to help you work toward those goals. How does that sound to you?
That sounds really good. Thank you for being willing to help me. I really do hope I can change this situation and not be bothered by this “dark shadow” anymore.
That sounds great. Let’s work together toward that goal. To start, we can try some ways to better manage and regulate your emotions. Would you be willing to try that with me?
Of course I’m willing to. To get rid of this feeling of being so weighed down, I’m willing to try all kinds of things.

Okay, then we can start with some simple mood tracking—writing down how your emotions change each day and what events trigger them. At the same time, we can also learn some relaxation techniques, like deep breathing exercises. How would you feel about trying these approaches first?
Okay, I’m willing to give the emotion log and deep breathing exercises a try. This might be a good place to start.

Wonderful. Today let’s start with an emotion log and some deep-breathing practice. You can spend a few minutes each day noting down what you’re feeling and what might have triggered it, and then try using deep breathing to ease those heavy, bottled-up feelings. If you have any questions or reactions, you can tell me anytime. I’m right here with you in this.
Hi
Hi there. What would you like to talk about today?
I’d like to talk about my relationship with a guy—he’s my dance partner.
Okay. Can you tell me what kinds of problems have come up between the two of you?
We’re dance partners and classmates, and we train together a lot. He’ll have some physical, kind of intimate contact with me usually, but I really can’t figure out what he actually thinks.
Got it. Do you feel confused or uncomfortable with this kind of physical closeness from him?
I’m a bit confused, because I once confessed my feelings to him, but he turned me down and said he needs to focus on dance right now.
And after that, he kept having close, intimate contact with you, right? That kind of behavior left you feeling confused. Do you feel like this might affect your dance partnership?
Yeah. After I confessed, we actually had a fight about it, and for a while he wouldn’t talk to me. I’m worried all this might affect our work together.
It sounds really tough. Have you talked with him directly about these worries at all? For example, letting him know that you want to protect your working relationship.
We haven’t really talked about it directly. After I confessed, his attitude was really awkward. We’re the kind of people who don’t chat normally and only talk when we see each other in person.
Mm. So within the way you two get along right now, finding a suitable moment to talk with him, or maybe writing him a letter to clearly express your feelings and worries—might that be an option?
I’ve thought about it, but every time I want to talk with him, he either picks on me or we end up snapping at each other. It feels really hard to have a serious conversation.

It does sound like the communication between you two is pretty tense. Have you tried a different way, like using text or messages, to see if that might make it easier to share your feelings and thoughts?
I actually have thought about texting him, but I’m really not sure how he’d react, and I’m afraid he might feel really awkward about it.

That really is a challenge. Maybe you could first try sending him a message in a more relaxed tone, just saying you’d like to have a proper conversation with him and handle the cooperation well. He might find it easier to accept that. How does that sound to you?
Maybe saying it this way would be better. I can give it a try. I just hope he can understand what I mean.
Yes, I hope the two of you can have some good communication and understanding. If there’s any progress, or if you run into any problems, you’re always welcome to come and talk with me.

Okay, thank you. Actually, there’s something else I’m confused about: every night he plays games with another girl, and he even mentions her in his status. That leaves me not really knowing what to do.
I see. It sounds like this situation leaves you feeling a bit confused and even uneasy. Do you feel that his interactions with that girl might affect your relationship?
I’m a bit worried, because he keeps messing with me, but then he mentions that girl in his status, so I really don’t know what he’s thinking.
These mixed messages really can be confusing. How would you feel about talking with him about your feelings and worries, to see if that might help you understand what he really thinks?
It might be a way, but I don’t know how to bring it up. I’m afraid it’ll make him feel like I’m interfering in his private life.

This really is something that’s worth thinking about. Maybe you could start from your own feelings, and let them know you’re not trying to interfere, but that you genuinely care about the relationship between you and would like to have a clearer understanding. Do you think it might be a bit easier to bring it up that way?
Maybe it would be better to put it this way: I’ll try to start from how I feel myself and spell out what I’m worried about.

Mm, it sounds like you already have a pretty good sense of direction. I hope you two can really talk things through and work out some of this confusion. If you need anything, you can come back and talk with me anytime.
Thank you. I’ll find a good time to sit down and talk with him properly and see if we can sort these things out.
Alright, I hope everything goes smoothly. If anything new comes up, you’re always welcome to come back and talk.
Hi
Hi, I’m Xiaotian. Would you like to talk about what’s been troubling you lately?
Hi. Lately I’ve been feeling really troubled about my relationships with people.
Mm, could you tell me a bit more about what kind of distress it is? Is it connected to certain people or situations?
I’ve noticed that when I’m interacting with people I’m not very close to, I’ll subconsciously keep my distance. This is actually a pretty common issue for me; it happens in any setting.
It sounds like you feel a bit uncomfortable when you’re around strangers. In those situations, do you usually feel tense or uneasy?
Yeah, it makes me feel really tense and uneasy. And a lot of the time I don’t even realize I’m feeling that way.

This tension and uneasiness you’re feeling may have a source. Can you think back to whether you’ve had similar experiences before, or any particular situations that tend to bring up these feelings for you?
I remember going through some upheaval when I was a kid, and maybe that’s when this kind of automatic defensiveness started.

Some of the changes you went through as a child might be affecting how you react emotionally now. Would you be willing to share a bit more about what those changes were? That way I can understand your situation better.
Honestly those changes are really blurry in my mind. I don’t really remember the exact details anymore, but I just have this sense they were things that made me feel unsafe.

I hear you. That kind of vague sense of insecurity may have really left a mark on you. Maybe we can start from what you’re going through right now and see if there are certain situations or people that especially set off this tension and uneasiness. What are those triggers for you?
Like when I get called on to speak in class, or when we’re discussing something in a group, I get really nervous, like everyone has these really high expectations of me.

When you’re noticed in class, you feel nervous, and this sense that a lot is expected of you brings up pressure and uneasiness. Do you feel like these expectations are coming from what other people are actually asking of you, or more from thoughts inside yourself?
I feel like it’s more about what’s going on in my own mind, like I just have this sense that people might be judging me.

These self-judging thoughts really can make a person feel tense and uneasy. Do you remember any specific situations where you felt that others clearly judged you, or has this feeling just kind of been there for as long as you can remember?
It’s like this feeling has always been there. People might not really be judging me, but I’m always worried about it.
This kind of ongoing worry really can come from some deeper feelings of insecurity inside. Have you tried any ways to ease your tension in those situations?
Sometimes I try taking deep breaths, or I try my best not to pay too much attention to the people around me, but it doesn’t really seem to help much.

Taking deep breaths and trying to shift your attention are good attempts, but they might not be enough on their own. We can try exploring some more effective approaches together, like changing how you see the situation, or finding ways that help you feel safe and confident. How would you feel about trying that together?
Okay, I’m willing to give it a try. Could you talk a bit about what kinds of approaches you think might help me?

We can try some cognitive restructuring tools, for example reminding yourself when you feel tense that not everyone is judging you. Also, you can experiment with gradually increasing how often you interact with people, starting with small, low‑pressure situations and slowly building your confidence, so you can feel more relaxed in those moments. How do you feel about trying something like this—do you think it might be helpful for you?
Um, I think I can give it a try. Gradually increasing how often we interact does seem like it could help.

Then we can start with some small goals, like saying a quick hello to one classmate each day, or trying to answer one question in class. Through these small attempts, you can gradually help yourself get more used to social situations step by step. How does that approach feel to you?
I think I can accept that. Starting with small goals, it doesn’t seem quite so hard.

That’s great. Starting step by step will help you gradually build confidence. As you go, try to notice your own progress and how you feel. Any new experiences or difficulties, you can share them with me, and we’ll adjust and fine-tune things together. Do you feel ready to start giving it a try?
Okay, I’m ready. I’ll try to hit these small goals every day.
Wonderful. I believe you can do this. If you have any new experiences or feelings, let me know anytime and we’ll look at them together and make adjustments. I’m rooting for you.
Hi
Hi, what’s been on your mind lately that you’d like to talk about with me?
I’d like to talk about how lost I’ve been feeling about my life lately.
Okay. Can you tell me a bit about what’s been making you feel lost? Is it work, relationships, or something else?
Mainly it’s work. I’m doing 9-9-6 every day, just repeating the same things over and over, and it all feels meaningless.
It sounds like you’re feeling really tired and bored with your current job. Can you tell me what parts of this job feel especially hard for you right now?
The work itself is really stifling. I’m facing pressure and negativity every single day, and I just feel completely exhausted, body and mind.
How are things in your work environment and with your coworkers? Do you feel like these factors have a big impact on you?
The work environment is okay, and my relationships with coworkers are so-so, but none of that seems to help much. I still just feel really tired.
I hear you. When you’ve been feeling this way, have you tried anything yourself to ease some of the stress and exhaustion?
Um, I’ll exercise or watch a movie once in a while, but it doesn’t really help. After a bit I just feel exhausted again.
These approaches are helpful ways to ease things a bit, but they might only be temporary. Have you ever thought about what’s made you lose your motivation and sense of meaning in your current job?
Maybe it’s because I don’t see any real sense of achievement. It just feels like the work is mechanically repeated and doesn’t have any real meaning.

A sense of accomplishment really is important for a person’s motivation. Have you ever had a similar feeling before? Or has there been any job or activity that made you feel especially accomplished and fulfilled?
It feels like there’s no work or activity that really gives me a sense of achievement. I’ve been fighting so hard for these goals all along, but it always feels like nothing has really changed.
When do you feel this started to become especially strong for you? Has it been just recently, or has this feeling been there for a long time already?
Probably about the past year or so, it’s been especially obvious. Before, even though the pressure was heavy, I still felt like there was a bit of hope.
Has anything particular happened recently, or have there been any changes in some areas of your life that have made this feeling stronger or more noticeable?
There wasn’t any big specific event. It’s just the day‑in, day‑out work piling on so much that I can hardly breathe, and I’ve been slowly feeling worse and worse.

Doing the same work over and over and being under constant high pressure really can leave you feeling exhausted and hopeless. Have you thought about looking for some new challenges, or trying something else you’re interested in, to help spark your motivation again?

Sometimes I do think about it, but I’m always worried it wouldn’t be stable. After all, my parents have pretty high expectations of me, and I’m afraid if I change jobs the pressure in my life will just get even heavier.

I can understand your concerns. The need for a stable life and your parents’ expectations really can bring a lot of pressure. In your current work situation, are there any small changes or new things you could try that feel at least somewhat doable and not too risky?
Maybe I could try finding some small challenges at work, or work on improving some skills, but it still feels really hard to change the overall suffocating atmosphere.

It’s true that changing the overall atmosphere might take some bigger adjustments. So, besides building your skills and looking for challenges, what other things do you think you could try to improve, to raise the quality of your work and your life? For example, building better connections with your coworkers, or developing some hobbies and interests outside of work.
Maybe I could try interacting more with my coworkers, or find some hobbies to get into, to take my mind off things. But I’m still worried I won’t have enough time or energy.

It sounds like you do have some ideas about making changes, but time and energy are a big issue. In that case, have you thought about starting with some small steps, like setting aside a little bit of time each week to do something you enjoy just for yourself? Even if it’s just a tiny part of your week, it might still bring about some changes.
Mm, that actually sounds like a good idea. I could try to set aside some time each week to do things I enjoy and let myself relax a bit. I’m not sure if that would make things a little better or not.

It’s always worth giving it a try. Small changes like these might help you find a bit more balance in the middle of your busy work. You can set some small goals for yourself and adjust things little by little, and see how that feels. I’m looking forward to hearing how it goes for you and what it’s like afterward.
Hi
Hi, what would you like to talk about today?
I’d like to talk about my relationship issues.
Okay. Could you tell me a bit more about it? What kind of difficulties have you been running into in your relationships lately?
I’ve been with my boyfriend for two years, but lately we keep arguing and even getting physical.
It sounds like things between you two are a bit tense right now. What do you think has been causing so much conflict between you lately?
I’m always testing whether he really loves me, and sometimes I even pretend I don’t love him that much, because I’m afraid of getting hurt.
I see, so in this way you’re trying to protect yourself from getting hurt in the relationship. How do you feel this way of handling things affects your connection with each other?
This way of doing things makes us argue a lot, and the physical fights are getting more and more frequent.

It seems like this way of doing things has really brought a lot of negative impact to your relationship. So, if you feel okay about it, how would you feel about trying some different ways of handling things between you two? For example, sharing your real feelings instead of testing whether the other person loves you?
I want to try, but I just can’t control myself. My longing for love and my insecurity are just too strong.
I hear how you’re feeling, and that sense of insecurity really is hard to manage. Can you remember when this feeling started, or whether anything in particular might have triggered it?
My parents were really busy when I was little, they didn’t have much time to be with me. I think that might be the reason.
It sounds like your upbringing has had some impact on your relationships now. How do you feel their being so busy and not really being around has affected you emotionally?
I feel really lonely, and I’m always longing for someone who can give me a sense of safety and love.

This sense of loneliness and longing for love is indeed a very deep emotional experience. In your relationships, what do you think you could do to help build more mutual understanding and trust, so that you can feel more secure?
Maybe I need to express my feelings more honestly, instead of constantly testing his love.

This is a really good start. Honestly expressing your feelings can help the other person understand you better, and it also helps build deeper trust. What are some specific ways you think you could try to express how you really feel?
I can try to calm myself down before we start arguing, and then tell him my real thoughts and feelings in a calmer tone.

This is a really positive step. After you’ve calmed down, sharing your true feelings in a calm tone can help reduce misunderstandings and conflict. Would you be willing to set some small goals for yourself, like reminding yourself to cool down first whenever there’s an argument, and then express how you feel?
I’m willing to try setting goals like that and hope things can get better.

Good, setting small goals is a great way to start. If you run into any difficulties along the way, you can always come to me and we can explore together how to further improve your emotional relationships. What are you hoping for in the future?
I really hope our relationship can become more stable and harmonious, and that we won’t keep arguing and fighting all the time.

That’s a really good goal. You’re already actively making efforts to improve the relationship, and if you take it step by step, I believe things between you can get better. What other areas do you think you might adjust or work on to help you move toward that goal?
I feel like we need to communicate more, and maybe we could also try doing some things together to deepen our connection. At the same time, I need to learn how to manage my own emotions better.

Those are all really good ideas. Increasing communication and doing more things together can help deepen your connection, and learning to manage your emotions will also have a positive impact on the stability of the relationship. Would you be willing to make some concrete plans around these goals? For example, setting up one in-depth conversation or shared activity each week, and adding in some emotional management exercises.

Okay, I can try setting up one deep conversation a week, or doing something we both enjoy together, like watching a movie or going for a walk. And I can also look for some ways to manage my emotions and practice those.

That sounds like a really good plan. Having a deep conversation and doing something together once a week can help the two of you communicate and feel more connected, and practicing emotion regulation will strengthen your ability to handle conflicts. You’re already working toward improving the relationship, and I do believe things between you can get better. Is there anything you’d like to talk more about or any other support you’d like from me?
I feel like the key now is whether I can actually keep following through with these plans. I’m worried I’ll give up halfway. How can I stay motivated and keep working on improving our relationship?

Staying motivated really is a challenge. Maybe you could try a few things: set small, achievable goals so you can build up a sense of success step by step; share your thoughts and plans with your partner so you can support and gently hold each other accountable; and keep track of each bit of progress and improvement, so you can see the positive impact of the changes. At the same time, you can also review and adjust your plan regularly to keep it flexible. Do you feel like any of these might be helpful for you?

These ideas sound really helpful. I’ll try to put them into practice. Especially sharing my thoughts with him, so we can support each other and keep each other on track. I feel like that way I’ll be more motivated to stick with it.

That’s great. Supporting and keeping an eye on each other can really help you stay motivated. Remember to keep communicating, adjust the plan in time when needed, and pay attention to every positive change, no matter how small. I trust that the two of you will work together to build a more stable and harmonious relationship. If you have any questions or need more support, you can always reach out to me. I’m rooting for you.

interaction.content: Hi
Hi there. How can I help you today?
I’d like to talk about my marriage.
Okay. Would you be willing to talk in a bit more detail about what’s troubling you in your marriage right now?
It’s mainly about whether or not to have kids.
This really is an important issue. Do you and your partner have different views about it?
Yeah, he wants kids, but I don’t.
I see. Could you share a bit about why you don’t want to have children?
Honestly I’m not even really sure myself, it’s just that deep down I keep feeling like I’ll end up divorcing him, so I don’t want to have kids tying us together.
It sounds like you’re feeling a bit insecure about this marriage. Can you tell me more about why you think it might end in divorce?
Maybe it’s because, deep down, I feel like I don’t really love him at all, so I keep feeling this way.
So when you chose to marry him, what was that decision based on?
Back then I felt like he was pretty good, and he treated me well too, so we got married. But now it feels different.
Mm, that kind of shift in how you feel can often be really confusing. What do you think might be behind these changes?
After we got married, we started arguing about a lot of things, especially about the kids and about living together with his parents.
These issues really can easily lead to conflict. About your child living together with his parents, could you talk in more detail about how that has affected your relationship?

When it comes to kids, he feels he has to carry on the family line, but I don’t want to have children, and that makes us argue a lot. And living together with his parents also makes me really uncomfortable.
It sounds like all of this has been really stressful for you. When it comes to living with his parents, what specifically has been making you feel uncomfortable?
They interfere way too much in our lives, and I feel like I have no privacy or freedom.
That really can make someone feel quite uncomfortable. Have you talked with your partner about these feelings? If so, how did he respond?
We’ve talked about it, but he always feels like I’m just picking a fight and doesn’t understand how I feel.

In a situation like this, it really does make communication hard. Have you tried any other ways to express your feelings and needs, like choosing a time or approach that he might find easier to accept?
I’ve tried talking to him when things were relatively calm, but it still hasn’t gone very well. He still doesn’t really understand me.
That must have felt really discouraging for you. At this point, what would you like to get out of counseling?
I want to figure out what I should actually do, whether to stay in this marriage or choose divorce.

This is a really important decision. Maybe we can start by looking at the gap between what you were hoping for in this marriage and how it actually feels, and explore in what specific ways you feel unsatisfied. How would you feel about that?
Yeah… I feel like our connection, both sexually and emotionally, is getting weaker and weaker, and that’s one of the reasons I feel so unsatisfied.
A decrease in sexual intimacy and emotional connection really can affect how satisfied you feel in a marriage. Could you tell me more about how your relationship has changed in these two areas?

When we were dating it was still okay, but after getting married it’s gotten less and less—like once or twice a month, and sometimes we can even go two months without doing it at all. Emotionally I also feel like we’re getting more and more distant.

Mm, that kind of change can feel really painful. Have you tried talking with him about the decrease in your sex life and emotional connection, or looking for some ways to improve things in those areas?
We’ve talked about it, but he feels like there’s no problem. I don’t know how to make things better, and deep down I really resist having sex with him.

It sounds like this issue is really troubling you. What do you think is the specific reason you’re feeling this resistance toward him? Is it because you feel emotionally distant, or are there other factors?
The main reason is the emotional distance between us, and also his snoring is really bad, so we ended up sleeping in separate rooms, which has also affected our intimacy.

Growing emotionally distant and sleeping in separate rooms can definitely affect your sense of closeness. Besides his snoring and the emotional distance, are there any other specific situations that make you feel resistant toward him?
Maybe it’s also because we’re always arguing about whether the child should live together with his parents, and that’s made me start to feel resistant toward him.

I hear you—you’ve been feeling really troubled and resistant in the midst of these ongoing arguments. Do you think that if these arguments could lessen or even stop, your emotional connection and sense of intimacy would improve?
It might get better, but I still have a lot of concerns about having a child.
Your concerns really matter, and anything related to having a child is a major decision. Could you talk in more detail about what worries you when it comes to having a baby?

I’m worried that maybe I really don’t love him, and once we have a child it’ll be even harder to get a divorce. Also, I feel like the way our relationship is right now just isn’t suitable for raising a child.

It makes a lot of sense that you have these concerns. If the way your relationship is right now really makes you feel it’s not a good situation to raise a child, then the most important thing is to first work on the issues between the two of you. What do you feel your needs and expectations are in this marriage?
I hope for more understanding and support, and I also want more personal space. I don’t like his parents interfering.

What you’re needing here is very reasonable. In your conversations with him, have you tried clearly expressing these needs? For example, have you talked with him about how he could offer you more understanding and support, and also respect your personal space?
I’ve tried, but every time we talk about this he feels like I’m picking on his family, and he doesn’t really understand how I feel.

It really isn’t easy. Maybe you could try describing your feelings and needs in a more specific way, instead of only pointing out what’s wrong—for example, by talking about concrete situations and what you were feeling in those moments to explain where you’re coming from. Would you be willing to try that approach?
I’m willing to give it a try, but I don’t know if it’ll actually work, and I’m a bit worried it might even stir up more conflict.

It’s completely understandable that you’re worried. You might try sharing your feelings and needs at a time when you’re both relatively calm, and in a non-confrontational tone; that could lower the chances of conflict. If that feels hard to do, we can explore some specific ways and strategies for communicating together. How does that sound to you?
That actually sounds pretty good. I’m willing to give it a try. Could you walk me through exactly how I should say it?

Of course. First, you can choose a moment when he’s relatively calm emotionally, and then start with an “I feel…” sentence, for example:

“I feel like the closeness between us has gone down recently, and that makes me a bit sad and uneasy.”

Then you can describe your needs more specifically, like:

“I hope we can have more time together, to share our thoughts and feelings. That’s really important to me.”

Expressing it this way can make it easier for him to understand how you feel, instead of feeling like you’re blaming him. How would you feel about trying to express it this way?
Okay, I can try expressing my feelings and needs that way. I hope things can get a bit better.

That’s great. Being willing to give it a try is the first step. Remember to stay patient and gentle, and try to avoid bringing these things up when the other person is very emotional. If you run into difficulties, we can always talk again. You’re not facing this on your own.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try my best to do what you said. I do feel a bit lonely, but I hope things can get better.

I hear how you’re feeling, and I’m really glad you’re willing to try some new approaches. Whenever you need support or want to explore things further, we can always talk again. I hope things will start to get better.
Um, thank you for your care and support. I’ll do my best. If I need to, I’ll get in touch with you again.
You’re very welcome, I’m here for you. I hope everything goes smoothly, and we can pick up our conversation anytime.

interaction.content: Hi
Hello, how can I help you today?
I’ve been feeling really low lately and wanted to talk with you about it.
Okay. Would you be willing to share a bit about what’s been getting you down lately?
My son just started first grade in primary school recently, and I’ve sent him to a boarding school.
Sending a child to boarding school is a big decision. Are you feeling down mainly because of that, or are there other things that have been troubling you?
It’s mainly because of this. He went to boarding school for a week, and after he came back he really couldn’t adjust. He’s been very resistant and doesn’t want to go back to school anymore.
It sounds like you’re really worried about how your child is adjusting. Have you talked with him about what kinds of problems he’s been running into at school?
Yeah. He told me he really misses me, and even said things like he might as well just die. Hearing that made me feel really awful.
His reaction really is heartbreaking. Have you thought about any ways that might help ease his emotions during this period?
I tried to comfort him, but he was still really worked up. He even hit me and bit me, asking why I sent him to boarding school.

It sounds like he feels really uncomfortable and scared about the boarding school. Have you thought about letting him stay at home a few more days, or finding some kind of middle-ground solution, like spending part of the time at the boarding school and part of the time at home?

I’ve thought about that too, but I’m worried that if we pull him out of the boarding school, it might have some impact on him psychologically. After all, he used to be such an independent, sensible kid.

It makes sense that you’re worried. Before you make a final decision, maybe you could try talking more with your child to understand what specific problems he’s been having at the boarding school, and see how you might help him gradually adjust to the new environment. That would also give you a chance to see whether his mood is improving. How does that approach sound to you?

I think we can give it a try. Actually, I’ve talked with his teacher too, and the teacher said he’s doing okay at school, but what he tells me is completely different. It leaves me not really knowing what to do.

In this situation, maybe you could try talking with your child and see if you can come up with some concrete ways to work on the problem together. For example, would it be possible to set up a gradual adjustment plan, or add some support systems for him at school so he can feel more secure? How would you feel about talking with him about these possible options?
I’m willing to give it a try, but I still feel really anxious and guilty inside, and I’m afraid I’ve made the wrong choice.

Your anxiety and self-blame show that you care a lot about your child. At the same time, every decision comes with a period of adjustment. Maybe you can also give yourself some time and try not to be so hard on yourself. The best thing you can do for your child right now is to support him through this adjustment period. What do you think might help you relax a bit more?
I’ve tried to relax, but I keep thinking about the kids, and I just don’t know how to really relax.

That’s completely understandable, especially as a parent—it’s not easy to put down your worries about your child. When you feel especially anxious, have there been any activities or methods that helped you feel even a little bit lighter? For example, taking some deep breaths, listening to music, or talking with a friend?

Listening to music helps a bit sometimes, but it doesn’t last very long. I also talk with my friends, and they all say there’s nothing wrong with choosing a boarding school, but I’m still worried about my child.

Support from friends is really important, but in the end you still need to find ways of coping that work for you. Maybe you could try limiting your “worry time” to a specific period each day, and then use the rest of the time to focus on things you enjoy. That might gradually ease some of the pressure. How do you feel about this idea—do you think it could be helpful for you?
That sounds like a good idea, I can give it a try. But I still can’t help worrying sometimes, like before bed at night, my mind just starts racing.

That’s a very normal reaction. For the anxiety you feel at night before bed, you can try some relaxation techniques to ease it. For example, you could keep a journal, write your worries down, give yourself a set time and space to worry, and then decide on a specific time to stop. Or you could try relaxation exercises like deep breathing or meditation. Have you tried any of these approaches before?
I haven’t really tried keeping a journal before, maybe I could give it a shot. I’ve heard of deep breathing and meditation, but I’ve never actually done them.

You can try these and see whether they work for you. Keeping a journal can help you sort out your thoughts, and deep breathing and meditation can help relax your body and mind. If you’d like to get into the specifics of how to do these relaxation exercises, I can offer some suggestions. Which one would you like to start with?
I think keeping a journal might be easier for me to try. I can try writing things down every night and see if it helps ease my anxiety a bit.

That sounds like a good start. Try spending a few minutes each night writing down your anxiety and feelings from the day, and you can also note a few things you feel grateful for. This can not only help you release some stress, but also gradually build a more positive way of thinking. How does that sound to you?
I think that could work. Maybe it’ll help me sort out my thoughts a bit and ease some of the pressure. I’ll try to write something every night.

This really is a brave decision. Give yourself some time to adjust and try out these new approaches, and I believe you’ll gradually start to see the effects. If you run into any problems along the way or need some extra support, you can always talk with me.
Okay, thank you for understanding and for your suggestions. I’ll try to stick with it, and if anything comes up I’ll let you know.
You’re very welcome. I’ll be here to support you. I hope that in the process of writing in your journal every day, you can find some inner calm and strength. You’ve got this.
Hi
Hi, I’m Xiaotian. How are you feeling today?
Hi, Xiaotian. I’m feeling okay today, just still a bit troubled. How about you?
I’m doing well, thank you for asking. You mentioned you’ve been feeling troubled—could you tell me more about what’s been bothering you?
Lately I keep getting into conflicts with my parents, especially my mom. I just always feel like she’s blaming me for things I didn’t do.
It sounds like things have been a bit tense between you and your mom lately. Could you tell me what happened that led to the conflict?
She’s always suspicious that I’ve done something wrong, and a while ago we had another big fight because of my ex.
Can you tell me more specifically how the situation with your ex-boyfriend led to arguments between you and your mom?
When we were together, my ex-boyfriend was always telling my parents I wasn’t a good person, saying I was materialistic and willful. And then after we broke up, my mom actually believed what he said.

It sounds like you’re feeling really wronged, that your mom believed what your ex-boyfriend said, and that’s left you feeling misunderstood. Have you ever tried talking with your mom calmly about it, and explaining how you feel and where you’re coming from?
I’ve tried, but every time I explain, she thinks I’m lying and says I’m not reflecting on myself.
In this situation, do you feel the main difficulty in communicating comes more from her attitude, or more from a lack of mutual understanding between the two of you?
I think it’s mainly her attitude. She always thinks she’s right and refuses to listen to my explanation.

It sounds like that attitude leaves you feeling powerless and defeated. In this kind of atmosphere, have you tried any other ways to help your mom understand how you feel? For example, writing her a letter, or inviting a neutral family member to join the conversation.
I tried writing her a letter, but she didn’t really care and even felt like I was just making excuses. I asked my dad to help talk to her, and then she felt like my dad was taking my side.
It sounds like you’ve tried a lot of different ways, but the results haven’t been very good. In this situation, what do you feel is the biggest impact that the conflict with your mom has on you?
The biggest impact is that I feel like I’m always being rejected or shot down, that whatever I do is wrong, and my emotions have become really unstable.

Feeling rejected really does hurt, and it can affect your mood and your confidence. Have you found any ways to work through those feelings, or to get support from elsewhere? For example, from friends or other family members?
Sometimes I talk with friends and feel a bit better, but I still feel like the root of all this is at home, so there’s only so much my friends can do.

It’s really important that your friends can understand and support you, but you’re also very clear that the root of the problem is at home. Have you thought about getting professional support outside the family, like seeing a counselor? They can help you work through these complicated feelings and relationships.
I have actually thought about it, but I’m also a bit scared, and I don’t know if counseling can really help me.

It’s completely understandable to feel worried—coming to counseling for the first time does take some courage. Counseling can offer you a safe space to better understand your own feelings and to cope with the challenges in your family relationships. You might try a few sessions first and see how it feels. What do you think?
That does kind of make sense, maybe it’s worth a try. After all, the way things are now really isn’t good, and trying it might help.

Going into this with a “let me just try” attitude is a really good start. The counselor will respect your pace and help you gradually understand and work through things. You’ve already taken an important first step, and I believe you’ll find better ways to cope with these challenges. If you’d like, you can keep talking with me, and we can also explore some coping strategies together.
Okay, thank you. I still have a lot I want to talk about, and I feel like I’ll feel a bit better if I can get it out.
Of course. I’m here to listen. You can take your time. Putting those bottled-up feelings into words can help you feel a bit lighter. What else would you like to share?

I think what hurts the most is feeling like I’ve never really been trusted since I was little, always being doubted and blamed for things I didn’t do. It makes me feel like I have no place at all in my own family.

Feeling constantly suspected and wrongly blamed is really painful, especially in your own home. Have you ever thought about whether these trust issues might come from certain specific events, or from the way your family communicates?
I’ve wondered if maybe my mom’s expectations for me are just too high, like I can never meet her standards. But I really have tried so hard, and I’m still not recognized.

Hearing that you’ve put in so much effort and still don’t feel recognized is really painful. There’s a big conflict between your mom’s high expectations and your own efforts. What kind of support or changes do you feel you would need so that you can adjust your emotions a bit better in this situation?
I feel like I need more self-affirmation and recognition, and maybe I can find a way to make myself stronger inside, so I won’t care so much about what my mom thinks.

That’s a really good direction. Building up your self-acceptance and inner strength can give you more power to face pressure from the outside world. Have you thought about some concrete ways you might strengthen your self-acceptance and inner resilience? For example, through hobbies, exercise, or mindfulness practices?
I’ve thought about trying to sort out my emotions by keeping a journal, and I’ve also been trying to do more things I enjoy, like drawing and exercising. It does feel a bit better.

Those sound like really good approaches. Journaling, drawing, and exercise are all great ways to regulate your emotions. You have a strong sense of self-awareness, and if you keep at these, they’ll gradually strengthen you on the inside. If any new feelings or difficulties come up along the way, you can always talk with me about them.
Okay, thank you for your support. I’ll keep trying to stick with these approaches, and I also hope that through talking with you I can find more ways to cope and some comfort.

You’re very welcome. The fact that you’ve been sticking with this and making your own adjustments is already really good progress. We can keep talking and look for more approaches that fit you, so you can feel better both emotionally and mentally. If you need anything, just let me know anytime.
Okay, thank you. I’ll keep trying, and I also hope that through talks like this I can find more support and ways to work things out.

Keeping this positive mindset is really important, and I trust you’ll keep finding ways that work for you to handle these challenges. We can keep talking about this—whenever there’s something you’d like to go into more deeply, just let me know.
Okay, I’d like to go a bit deeper into my relationship with my mom—why she’s always so domineering, and whether there’s any way for her to understand me a bit more.

Your mom’s being so forceful might be her way of communicating, or her way of showing she cares about you. If you want her to understand you more, you could try gradually building a more effective way of communicating with her. In what kinds of situations do you feel she’s more willing to really listen to you?
I feel like when she’s in a better mood, she’s relatively more willing to listen to me. And also, if my dad can be there, sometimes that helps ease things a bit too.

That’s a really good observation. Choosing to talk with your mom when she’s in a better mood, or when your dad is there too, really might make the conversation go more smoothly. Would you be willing to try sharing your feelings and thoughts with her again in those moments?
I’m willing to give it a try, but I’m still a bit worried she won’t listen. But if I don’t try, I won’t know if it works, so I’ll look for a chance to try it out.

It’s completely normal to have this kind of worry, and being willing to give it a try is already a really good start. Whatever the outcome, you’ll be able to learn something from it and find better ways to communicate. If anything comes up along the way, just let me know anytime and we can look at it together.
Okay, thank you. I’ll try my best to talk with her. If I run into any problems, I’ll come back and talk with you again.
I’ll be here to support you. Keep going—trust that you’ll find better ways to communicate. You’re always welcome to come back and talk.
Hi
Hi, it’s good to see you. Shall we get started? Have you run into anything lately that’s been bothering you?
Um, yeah. Lately there’s this guy in my class who keeps sneaking looks at me and smiling at me, and I feel like I’ve started paying attention to my appearance again, like I did before.
It sounds like this guy’s behavior is bothering you a bit. You mentioned “like before” — could you tell me more about what happened before?
So, in my second year of high school there was this boy who confessed his feelings to me. I was really happy at the time, but I still turned him down, because I felt really inferior.
It sounds like that experience had quite a big impact on you. Where does your sense of inferiority come from? Is it connected to some things that happened in the past?
I guess so. Ever since I was little, almost no one has liked me. I feel like I’m a really boring person.
I hear you. That feeling can be really painful. Maybe we can try to sort it out a bit—when you say you feel boring, what specific parts of yourself are you thinking about?
I feel like I’m not very good at expressing myself, and I’m also pretty withdrawn and timid, and not very confident socially.
Those feelings really can make you doubt yourself. Have you ever had any experiences that made you feel confident or happy?
Yeah. Back in my second year of high school, when someone confessed to me, I was actually really happy inside. I felt like I was someone who could be liked.
That experience of being confessed to helped you feel seen and valued. Besides that time, have there been moments when you felt you did something well and felt confident in yourself?
Um, I think I look okay, and sometimes people say I’m pretty. When that happens, I feel a bit more confident.

That’s great. Getting affirmation for your appearance is one part of it. We can also explore together how you might find more of your own value in other areas and build up your confidence. Have you tried different hobbies, or thought about developing some new skills?
I’ve tried, like with makeup. I really like doing my makeup, and when I get up early every day and spend time on it, I feel kind of elegant. But sometimes it also feels a bit tiring.

Makeup can boost your confidence, and feeling elegant is a really lovely thing. But if it’s making you feel tired, maybe there’s a balance you could find. Besides putting on makeup, are there other things that help you feel relaxed and happy?
For now, the only thing I can think of is listening to music. Sometimes it helps me feel a bit more relaxed.

Listening to music really is a great way to relax. We can also try out different hobbies and interests to find more things that make you feel happy and confident. Would you be interested in exploring some new areas, like reading, exercise, or doing some crafts?
Um, I’m kind of interested in doing crafts. When I see the little things other people make, I think they look pretty fun, but I haven’t really tried much myself.

Trying some kind of handicraft could be a really nice new experiment. It can not only give you the joy of creating something, but also help you build patience and focus. You could start with something simple, like braiding a bracelet or making small decorations, and slowly find your own rhythm and feel for it. How does that sound to you?
That sounds pretty good. I can try out some of those simple crafts.

That’s great. Trying new things can really help build your confidence, and it’s also a way to explore yourself. You can take it slowly, there’s no need to put too much pressure on yourself—just focus on enjoying the process. And if you have any new experiences or feelings, you’re welcome to share them with me anytime.
Okay, thank you for the suggestion. I’ll try doing some crafts and see if I can find some new enjoyment in it.

You’re very welcome. I hope you can find both enjoyment and a sense of accomplishment in your crafts. If you notice any new feelings or run into any confusion along the way, you can always come back and talk with me. Wishing you all the best.
Thank you. I’ll really try, and I hope I can find some new interests and confidence in myself.

You’ve got this. I believe you’ll find more things that make you feel happy and confident. If you ever want to talk about anything, you’re always welcome to come to me. I hope each step you take brings some positive change.
